summary: Same pattern — a fully-saturated single hue filling the strip over a linear index brightness ramp, hue rotating steadily — and at every explicitly-dialed sliderSpeed above ~0.4 the two sides are nearly pixel-identical; but the port's UNTOUCHED default runs 4.06x too slow (4.10 s per rainbow vs the original's 1.01 s), it lacks the original's rate quantization (original is fully frozen for speed <= ~0.12 while the port still creeps), and its brightness ramp uses i/(n-1) where the original uses i/n.
observations: Both sides render, no compile or runtime errors, no sensors bound (wantsSensors false on both), no seed dependence (seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give identical stats on both sides), no randomness.

Structure (both sides, identical): the whole strip shows ONE fully-saturated hue at any instant (B=0 while R/G rise, etc. — dumps confirm hue is uniform across pixel index), multiplied by a linear brightness ramp along the strip: pixel 0 is black, brightness rises monotonically to the far end. No bands, no travelling features — all motion is the hue walking through the colour wheel.

Motion is TIME-BASED on both sides: hue rate at sliderSpeed=0.5 measured 87.93 deg/s at 20 fps and 87.891 deg/s at 40 fps on BOTH sides (0.05% agreement), so neither side is frame-rate coupled. The `motion` stat scaling (orig 12@20fps -> 49@5fps; port 3@20fps -> 12@5fps) is the expected 1/fps scaling of a time-based pattern, identical in shape on both sides.

HEADLINE: untouched defaults diverge 4.06x. Untouched original hue rate = 357.06 deg/s (full rainbow every 1.008 s); untouched port = 87.90 deg/s (every 4.096 s). Measured by linear regression on unwrapped mean-RGB hue over a 6 s / 20 fps baseline and confirmed over 240 s. The original's untouched render is byte-for-byte the sliderSpeed=1 render; the port's untouched render is byte-for-byte its sliderSpeed=0.5 render — i.e. the port's internal default for sliderSpeed is 0.5 where the original's is 1.0.

DIALED comparison (the deciding evidence): with the same sliderSpeed set on both sides via --controls-orig/--controls-port, the sides agree closely. Measured hue rates (deg/s, orig vs port): v=0 -> 0.00 vs 0.00 (both frozen on pure red, mean brightness 42, motion 0); v=0.25 -> 21.973 vs 21.972; v=0.45 -> 71.411 vs 71.081; v=0.5 -> 87.891 vs 87.891; v=0.6 -> 126.343 vs 126.563; v=0.8 -> 225.220 vs 225.000; v=1 -> 357.056 vs 351.563. Above v~0.4 all agreements are within 2%.

The original's hue rate is QUANTIZED; the port's is continuous. The original only ever posts integer multiples of 5.4932 deg/s (= 1/65.536 cycles/s). Fitting the whole 0..1 sweep, the original's rate is exactly floor(65 * v^2) of those quanta, while the port's is a smooth 64 * v^2 quanta. Consequences: (a) the original is COMPLETELY FROZEN for v <= ~0.124 (measured 0.000 deg/s at v=0.05 and v=0.10) while the port rotates at 0.882 and 3.520 deg/s there; (b) low-mid settings mismatch materially — v=0.15: orig 5.497 vs port 7.801 (+42%); v=0.2: 10.987 vs 13.953 (+27%); v=0.3: 27.468 vs 31.642 (+15%); v=0.35: 38.452 vs 43.067 (+12%); (c) at the top of the slider the port is 1.54% SLOW (v=1: 357.06 vs 351.56), because the port's coefficient is 64 quanta/s where the original's peak lands on 65.

Brightness-ramp off-by-one. The original's ramp is 255*i/pixelCount; the port's is 255*i/(pixelCount-1). Dumps at sliderSpeed=0, t=0: on 12 px the original runs 0,21,42,63,84,106,127,148,169,191,212,233 while the port runs 0,23,46,69,92,115,139,162,185,208,231,255 (top pixel 233 vs 255, ~9% brighter port). On the default 60 px strip: orig pixel 29/58/59 = 123/246/250, port = 125/250/255 (~2% brighter port). On 300 px: 254 vs 255 (negligible). This shows up in every stats summary as port meanBrightness ~1.5% above orig (62.4 vs 63.5) and channel max 125 vs 127.

No regimes, no modes, no super-cycle. A 60 s / 5 fps survey and a 240 s / 10 fps survey (both sides dialed to 0.5) show a single continuous hue rotation with no banding boundaries; 30 s buckets of meanBrightness are flat on both sides (orig 62.3-62.4 [42-83] every bucket, port 63.4-63.5 [42-85] every bucket). brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, zeroMotionFrames 1 (the mandatory first frame) on both.

Steady state is healthy on both sides. A --skip 300 / 12 s / 20 fps late window shows orig motion avg 12.0 (min 12, max 13) and port motion avg 3.0 (min 3, max 3), zeroMotionFrames 0 on both, brightnessTrend 'steady' — neither side decays, freezes or saturates. The late-window motion gap is purely the untouched-default speed gap, not a dying port.

Phase stays locked over long windows when dialed the same: at sliderSpeed=0.5 after 240 s the two sides' mean RGB are orig 0/54/125 vs port 0/55/127 — same hue, no accumulated drift. At sliderSpeed=1 the 1.54% rate gap does accumulate: dumps show the sides near-identical at t=0 (mean abs pixel diff 0.76) drifting to ~22 deg of hue separation by t=4 s (mean abs diff 16.1).

Control surface matches exactly: both sides expose one control, name 'sliderSpeed', kind 'slider', label 'Speed'. Probe calls it responsive on both (orig maxDelta 62.88 / maxDeltaLit 63.94; port 64.97 / 66.07), and 0 vs 1 differ from each other on both sides, so it is genuinely value-dependent, not a setter artefact.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Sets the hue rotation rate. Quadratic in the slider value and QUANTIZED to multiples of 5.4932 deg/s (1/65.536 cycles/s): rate = floor(65 * v^2) quanta. v=0 freezes the strip on pure red; v stays frozen up to ~0.124; v=0.25 gives 21.97 deg/s (16.4 s per rainbow); v=0.5 gives 87.89 deg/s (4.10 s); v=1 gives 357.06 deg/s (1.008 s). Untouched default behaves exactly as v=1.
dials.portEffect: Same quadratic law and same direction, but CONTINUOUS (no quantization) and with coefficient 64 instead of 65 quanta: rate = 64 * v^2 quanta = 351.56 * v^2 deg/s. v=0 freezes on pure red (matches). v=0.05/0.10 still creep at 0.88/3.52 deg/s where the original is frozen. v=0.25 -> 21.97, v=0.5 -> 87.89, v=1 -> 351.56 deg/s. Untouched default behaves exactly as v=0.5, i.e. 4.06x slower than the original's untouched default.

feedback: PRIMARY FIX: the port's untouched default speed is half the original's. Untouched, the original completes a full rainbow every 1.008 s (357.06 deg/s) and the port takes 4.096 s (87.90 deg/s) — a 4.06x gap that is immediately obvious to a viewer. The port's untouched render is byte-identical to its own sliderSpeed=0.5 render, and the original's untouched render is byte-identical to its sliderSpeed=1 render, so the port's initial value for the speed control needs to move from 0.5 to 1.0 (or whatever internal quantity produces 357 deg/s untouched). Everything else about the untouched render already matches.

SECONDARY: the port's hue rate is ~1.54% slow at the top of the slider. At sliderSpeed=1 the original runs 357.06 deg/s and the port 351.56 deg/s. Expressed in the original's natural unit of 1/65.536 cycles per second, the original's peak is 65 units and the port's is 64. Scaling the port's rate coefficient by 65/64 makes v=1 land exactly on the original. This is invisible over a few seconds but accumulates to a visible ~22 deg hue offset by t=4 s and a full half-cycle by ~33 s.

TERTIARY (low-speed fidelity): the original quantizes the hue rate to integer multiples of 5.4932 deg/s — measured rate = floor(65 * speed^2) quanta across a 20-point sweep — while the port's rate is smooth. The visible consequence is that the original is FULLY FROZEN for any speed setting at or below ~0.124 (0.000 deg/s at v=0.05 and v=0.10) whereas the port keeps creeping (0.88 and 3.52 deg/s), and the port runs 12-42% fast through the v=0.15..0.35 range (v=0.15: 5.50 vs 7.80; v=0.2: 10.99 vs 13.95; v=0.3: 27.47 vs 31.64). If the port is meant to reproduce the original's low-speed feel, its rate needs to be floored to the same 1/65.536 cycles-per-second grid. Above v~0.4 the quantization error is under 2% and this stops mattering.

MINOR (off-by-one in the brightness ramp): the original's per-pixel brightness scale is index/pixelCount, the port's is index/(pixelCount-1), so the port's last pixel is always full 255 while the original's never quite reaches it. On 12 px the top pixel is 233 (orig) vs 255 (port), a 9% gap; on the default 60 px it is 250 vs 255; on 300 px 254 vs 255. Dividing by the pixel count rather than count-1 removes the persistent ~1.5% whole-strip brightness offset seen in every stats summary.

No other changes needed: spatial structure (uniform saturated hue over a linear index ramp), hue direction (increasing/red->green->blue), palette (full-saturation rainbow, both sides reach channel extremes with the third channel at 0), colour distribution, steady state over 240 s, fps-invariance, seed-independence and the control surface (one slider named sliderSpeed) all already match.
